title: Interval tensors preserve cosimplicial resolutions and presentable terms
statement:
Use the universes of [def-coef-complete-algebroid] and the complete, cocomplete model-category, weak-equivalence, cofibrant-object and Reedy terminology of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. A cosimplicial resolution means a Reedy cofibrant functor $A^\bullet:\Delta\to\mathcal M$ whose structure maps are weak equivalences. Its canonical augmentation to $\operatorname{const}(A^0)$ is induced by the unique maps $[n]\to[0]$. For a simplicial set $K$ of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], define $A^\bullet\otimes_\Delta K=\int^{[r]\in\Delta}A^r\cdot K_r$, with copower $Z\cdot S=\coprod_{s\in S}Z$, and define the cosimplicial tensor by
$$(A^\bullet\otimes K)^m=A^\bullet\otimes_\Delta(K\times\Delta^m).$$
The coend is the coproduct modulo the relations from simplex operators, and $\Delta^m$ is the representable standard simplex. These constructions are functorial in $A,K$. If $A^\bullet$ is a cosimplicial resolution, then $A^\bullet\otimes\Delta^1$ is a cosimplicial resolution, and the two endpoint inclusions induce natural objectwise weak equivalences $e_0,e_1:A^\bullet\to A^\bullet\otimes\Delta^1$, using $A^\bullet\otimes\Delta^0\cong A^\bullet$. If $\lambda$ is an infinite regular cardinal and all terms of $A^\bullet$ are $\lambda$-presentable (their Hom functors preserve $\lambda$-filtered colimits), the same holds for the terms of $A^\bullet\otimes\Delta^1$. No simplicial enrichment of $\mathcal M$ is assumed.

source.place: Appendix A.1 and proof of Lemma 6.4, printed pp. 191, 197; Hovey, Model Categories, Propositions 5.4.1, 5.4.3 and Corollary 5.4.4, printed pp. 129-131. Presentability follows from the finite nondegenerate-simplex decomposition of Delta^1 times Delta^m. No Stacks tag states this cosimplicial-frame fact. Sources read online 2026-10-17, not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Put $V_A(K)=A^\bullet\otimes_\Delta K$. In the cocomplete category of the statement this is the coequalizer $\coprod_{\theta:[r]\to[s]}A^r\cdot K_s\rightrightarrows\coprod_r A^r\cdot K_r$, with arrows induced by $A(\theta)$ and $K(\theta)$. Maps from it to $Z$ are exactly families $K_r\to\operatorname{Hom}(A^r,Z)$ compatible with simplex operators; hence $V_A$ is left adjoint to $Z\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(A^\bullet,Z)$ and preserves small colimits. For $K=\Delta^m$, the summand indexed by $\alpha:[r]\to[m]$ maps to $A^m$ by $A(\alpha)$; the coend relations identify this with the identity summand in degree $m$, giving $V_A(\Delta^m)\cong A^m$. For $\partial\Delta^m$, every simplex $\alpha:[r]\to[m]$ has proper image and factors uniquely as a surjection onto that image followed by a proper injective face. The coend relation for this surjection reduces its summand to that face, and relations between faces are precisely their face inclusions. Thus its coend is the colimit over proper injective faces, namely $L_mA$; for $m=0$ both indexing diagrams are empty. These identifications are natural. Maps of $A$ and $K$ induce maps of the displayed coequalizers; composition and identities hold on every summand. Thus $B^m=V_A(K\times\Delta^m)$ defines a cosimplicial functor, functorial in both variables, and $A\otimes\Delta^0\cong A$.

source.place: Appendix A.1, printed p.197; explicit coequalizer universal properties and representable/boundary evaluation (Hovey Proposition 3.1.5).

proof.text: Assume $A$ is a cosimplicial resolution. By its Reedy cofibrancy the maps $V_A(\partial\Delta^m)\to V_A(\Delta^m)$ of step 1 are cofibrations, including the initial map in degree zero. The collapses $V_A(\Delta^m)\to V_A(\Delta^0)$ are precisely $A([m]\to[0])$, weak equivalences by the hypothesis on structure maps. The boundary-and-collapse criterion [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test] therefore applies to this colimit-preserving $V_A$: it sends monomorphisms to cofibrations and weak homotopy equivalences to weak equivalences, with no enrichment assumption on $\mathcal M$.

Take $K=\Delta^1$ and write $B=A\otimes\Delta^1$. The latching colimit in degree $m$ is $L_mB\cong V_A(\Delta^1\times\partial\Delta^m)$. Indeed $V_A$ preserves colimits, and product with a fixed set preserves colimits of sets: in the disjoint-union-and-relations description the first coordinate is unchanged by every relation. Apply this in every simplicial degree to the proper-face presentation of the boundary from step 1. The latching map is consequently $V_A(\Delta^1\times\partial\Delta^m)\to V_A(\Delta^1\times\Delta^m)$. Its input map is degreewise injective, so step 2 makes it a cofibration. For $m=0$ the boundary and the latching object are initial, and the same argument applies. Thus $B$ is Reedy cofibrant by [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure].

source.place: Proof of Theorem 5.5.3, printed p.134: the frame A tensor (K times Delta[-]); latching calculation written out.

proof.text: Each endpoint inclusion $\Delta^0\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ is a one-dimensional horn inclusion and hence has the left lifting property against every Kan fibration, by the definitions in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Apply [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product] with $i:\varnothing\to\Delta^m$ and $j$ equal to either endpoint. Its pushout-product is $\Delta^m\times\Delta^0\to\Delta^m\times\Delta^1$. It is anodyne, therefore a trivial cofibration in the Kan model structure: the left class against all fibrations is precisely the trivial cofibrations. In particular it is a weak homotopy equivalence. Applying $V_A$ and the weak-equivalence conclusion of [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test] gives both $e_i^m:A^m\to B^m$ as weak equivalences. The two maps are natural in $m$ and $A$ because all their components are induced by the same fixed endpoint maps in the functorial coequalizer of step 1.

source.place: Corollary 5.4.4, printed p.131; the simplicial-set pushout-product argument gives both endpoint maps, as required in Dugger Lemma 6.4.

proof.text: For any $\theta:[m]\to[n]$, naturality gives $B(\theta)e_0^m=e_0^n A(\theta)$. Both $e_0$ components and $A(\theta)$ are weak equivalences, so two-out-of-three makes $B(\theta)$ a weak equivalence. Combined with step 3 this says that $B$ is a cosimplicial resolution. Its augmentation is the functorial map induced by $[m]\to[0]$; the same composition identity proves naturality of this augmentation, and its components are weak equivalences. The argument has used ordinary coends and model-category axioms only.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 6.4, printed p.191: the interval-tensor endofunctor on cosimplicial resolutions and its endpoint natural transformations.

proof.text: Fix $m$. A simplex of $\Delta^1\times\Delta^m$ is an order-preserving sequence in the finite product poset $P=[1]\times[m]$. It is nondegenerate precisely when consecutive pairs are distinct, that is, when the sequence is a strict chain in $P$. Delete consecutive repetitions to obtain its unique strict chain and the unique order-preserving surjection onto that chain. Let $J_m$ be the finite poset of nonempty strict chains in $P$, ordered by face inclusion, and let $D_m$ send a chain of $r+1$ vertices to $A^r$, and a face inclusion to the corresponding injective simplex operator. Then $V_A(\Delta^1\times\Delta^m)\cong\operatorname{colim}_{J_m}D_m$. To check the isomorphism, maps from the right side to $Z$ are a compatible map $A^r\to Z$ for every strict chain. For a repeated sequence with surjection $\sigma:[s]\twoheadrightarrow[r]$, extend that map by precomposing with $A(\sigma):A^s\to A^r$. Explicitly write a repeated sequence as $x=c\sigma$, with $c:[r]\to P$ a strict chain and $\sigma:[s]\twoheadrightarrow[r]$. For $\theta:[t]\to[s]$, factor $\sigma\theta=\iota\tau$ with $\tau:[t]\twoheadrightarrow[q]$ surjective and $\iota:[q]\hookrightarrow[r]$ injective. The strict chain of $x\theta$ is $c\iota$, a face of $c$. If $u_c:A^r\to Z$ denotes the compatible chain map, face compatibility says $u_{c\iota}=u_c A(\iota)$, whence the extended map for $x\theta$ is $u_{c\iota}A(\tau)=u_c A(\sigma)A(\theta)$. This is exactly the coend relation for $\theta$. Restriction to strict chains and this extension are inverse, proving the asserted universal property. Since $P$ is finite, $J_m$ has finitely many objects and arrows; only finitely many terms of $A$ occur. This is a finite presentation of the term, despite the infinite indexing in the original coend.

source.place: Appendix A.1, coend formula, printed p.197; explicit finite strict-chain presentation for the product of two standard simplices (agent argument).

proof.text:
Let $\lambda$ be infinite regular as in the statement, $I$ a small $\lambda$-filtered category, and $X:I\to\mathcal M$ a diagram. Such an $I$ is filtered since finite diagrams have fewer than $\lambda$ morphisms. Put $Q=\operatorname{colim}_{J_m}D_m=B^m$. Its colimit universal property and the assumed $\lambda$-presentability of each $D_m(j)=A^r$, followed by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimits-commute-finite-limits], give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(Q,\operatorname{colim}_iX_i)\cong\lim_{j\in J_m^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Hom}(D_m(j),\operatorname{colim}_iX_i)\cong\lim_j\operatorname{colim}_i\operatorname{Hom}(D_m(j),X_i)\cong\operatorname{colim}_i\lim_j\operatorname{Hom}(D_m(j),X_i)\cong\operatorname{colim}_i\operatorname{Hom}(Q,X_i).$$
The limit category $J_m^{\mathrm{op}}$ is finite, so the cited theorem applies to sets, in the fixed Hom universe. The inverse of the displayed composite is the canonical preservation map: a class represented by $f:Q\to X_i$ is sent to its composite with $X_i\to\operatorname{colim}_iX_i$, since restricting this composite along each $D_m(j)\to Q$ gives the corresponding Hom comparison. Thus that canonical map is a bijection. Hence $B^m$ is $\lambda$-presentable for every $m$. The same proof covers $\lambda=\aleph_0$; no enlargement of the given regular cardinal is needed.
